r2_sort_region — 2D region op

• Data kinds: region → region

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "r2_sort_region", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

• HALCON equivalent: sort_region (the HALCON reference is a useful guide to its meaning and parameters)

Usage

Keep the k-th largest connected component; k = round(a*(n-1)).

Splits the foreground mask (> 0.5) into connected components with scipy.ndimage.label (default 4-connectivity), sorts them in descending order of area (pixel count), and keeps only the k-th component. k is the integer round(a*(n-1)) clipped to [0, n-1]: a=0 gives the largest component, a=1 the smallest, a=0.5 a component of roughly middle rank. n is the number of components. b is unused.

The return value is a float64 0/1 mask of the same shape as the input. All zeros if there are no components. When several components have the same area, their order is not guaranteed (it depends on the order of numpy.argsort). When the number of components n changes, the same a selects a different rank (relative specification), so if you just want to reliably get "the largest component", use a=0 or select_largest. Pixels connected only diagonally are counted as separate components (4-connectivity). Cutting constrictions upstream with opening_circle makes component-wise selection more stable.

Border handling: treat everything outside the image as background (0) (measured; tools/impl2/border_probe.py).
